First, I need to check the statement: "the only total that appears more than two times is 22." This means that among the "total" column values, the only value that occurs more than twice (i.e., three or more times) is 22. I need to see if any other total appears more than twice besides 22, or if 22 itself appears more than twice.

Looking at the "total" column in the table:

- 34 appears once (kotonishiki)
- 32 appears once (kaiō)
- 31 appears once (musōyama)
- 30 appears twice (hasegawa, kotomitsuki)
- 27 appears twice (akinoshima, takamiyama)
- 26 appears twice (takatōriki, wakanosato)
- 22 appears three times (daikirin, tochiazuma ii, kisenosato)

So, the counts:
- 34: 1 time
- 32: 1 time
- 31: 1 time
- 30: 2 times
- 27: 2 times
- 26: 2 times
- 22: 3 times

Now, "more than two times" means >2, so three or more times. Only 22 appears three times, which is more than two times. No other total appears more than two times (all others are 1 or 2 times). Therefore, the statement is true: the only total that appears more than two times is 22.

Final Answer: Yes
